text: The exact figure. Is $9,408,000 from the sales tax and $1,117,000 from the use tax.

speaker: elizabethforeman
text: How much of that do you know readily? How much of that is the SRO salaries?

speaker: anthonyfrancisco
text: Remembering that the SRO program is just one part of public safety sales tax, but the school resource officer salaries totaled last fiscal year, including overtime about $1.1 million.

speaker: elizabethforeman
text: Okay, so it's been inferred a lot and so I'm just gonna rip the bandaid off and say it. I mean, we see this as a problem, it's not sustainable. We just can't keep doing this. I think we have a big problem with trust and finances. So supplementing from the general fund every year, I think anybody can tell you, borrowing from your savings account is a bad plan or paying for things on credit, it's a bad plan operating right now. So I don't wanna kick the can down the road and like, oh, 2025, 2026, we're really gonna be in a pickle. I think we need to actually start talking about this now. I think we need to take it back to the public now. It's a very passionate issue. I know a lot of people want it. They don't wanna see the program suffer. And so I think we need to start having the discussions now to start putting this to a vote because this is just not sustainable for the city. And I know that people want this program. I think there's benefits to the program, doesn't necessarily feel good for some other people and we've had really great discussions about that. And I think we can keep having those discussions, but Anthony, Catherine, Darrell, I don't know who it would be but if we were to take this, I mean, what kind of like percentage increase, like how much would we need to get just to break even?

speaker: darrelpyle
text: So Anthony, the number that we had from the 1.8% for public transit, what does that generate annually? About 2.5 million. So we were overspent by 1.5 and an eighth of a percent gets you about 2.5 million. Now, if that projects out, so you're somewhere between an eighth and a quarter percent would be, I would assume adequate, but we would definitely do some analysis on that.

speaker: elizabethforeman
text: Okay, thank you.

speaker: breeaclark
text: Councilor Peacock.

speaker: mattpeacock
text: Yeah, Council Member Foreman just asked my question, but I do have another one. It's for Mr. Milner. Am I correct in understanding that bond funds cannot be used for salary?

speaker: justinmilner
text: That is correct. Bond funds cannot be used for salary. They're there for infrastructure materials.

speaker: mattpeacock
text: So there's no scenario in the future where this program could possibly be propped up with bond funds?

speaker: justinmilner
text: No, this could not be supplemented with use of school bond funds. And if, did I understand Mr. Francisco to say it was 1,100,000 total?

speaker: anthonyfrancisco
text: No, that was just the salaries and overtime for the SRO program. Remember that the SRO program is only one part of the public safety sales tax expense.

speaker: justinmilner
text: Yeah, I was just dividing that in half. And so it looked like maybe we, as Norman Public Schools were spending actually more than half as far as our share, because that would be 550,000 and ours we've been spending about 680,000. So I just wanted to make sure I understood that correctly.

speaker: anthonyfrancisco
text: Yeah, there has always been a lively debate when we go to the public schools each year to budget for what 50% will be. 50% of what? Is it 50% of just salary and overtime? Or is it 50% of the vehicle replacements and all of those other things that are involved in the program? So the decision has been salary related expenses and 50% of that.

speaker: mattpeacock
text: Well, I just wanna go ahead and yeah, echo the budgetary concerns of all my colleagues. I think those are very legitimate and fair. And I think a prudent action would be to go back to the people. So I'll leave it with that.

speaker: breeaclark
text: Mr. Milner, is it my understanding that the Norman Public Schools will not be able to contribute more? And I know you can't make that decision right now, but hopefully you've had the discussion. If we accept this grant, well, can we count on you to increase half of your half? And I asked that knowing that enrollment has got to be down with all of the online education that people are moving to for the reasons of a pandemic. And we don't know if they're gonna come back. And I know that our funding is based on per pupil. So I understand the concerns, but I mean, have you guys talked about that?

speaker: justinmilner
text: Yes, and unfortunately Dr. Millerino couldn't be here due to conflict with another meeting. But as I mentioned earlier, we weren't really part of the original conversation in February about, so those kinds of budget decisions had to be made early on, obviously pre-COVID. So to be able to be in the midst of a budget and be able to commit another, an additional amount above what we're already committed to, which I think it sounds like from the numbers we're above 50% already, would be somewhat impossible to do that with, as you mentioned, the enrollment going down, the COVID expenses going up and the like. So that's now past that, who's to be able to know and foretell the future, but in the midst of a budget coming up with that amount would be difficult.

speaker: breeaclark
text: Understood. Senior Manager Pyle, if we wanted to throw an election out there just to see what's going on, we know we have the road maintenance bond. We know we have water rate increase. This would be, and they're all different. So we got that going for us. This would be a sales tax increase, but just to let them decide, we would obviously have to make a decision about this grant before that time. But that seems like the obvious answer. What is a timeline that we could put something together and let the public speak?

speaker: darrelpyle
text: And I'll ask the city attorney to help me on my timing. So you have a couple of other questions that will be considered in the not too distant future, including recommendations from your charter review committee. And if, and city attorney is much better versed in terms of what types of questions can appear on the same ballot. So they don't all have to be on separate ballots. We could include several questions on the same one. So Ms. Walker, if you can clarify what types of questions we can have on the same ballot, that may really shorten the timeline.

speaker: kathrynwalker
text: Yeah, generally there's not a limitation with the exception of recall under our charter. Anything else could be set on the same election. We generally have to give 60 days notice to the election board. And so if you're adopting something by ordinance, which our sales tax ordinance would be for PSST, you've got to back that up to the first and second reading, and then preferably 30 days prior to the 60 day notice.

speaker: breeaclark
text: So Mr. Steeve, if we wanted to put this in April and it fails, can we say, hey, about that grant, I appreciate that you finally pulled our number and we were able to move forward, but we just can't afford it. I mean, is there a way to back out of it at that point?

speaker: darrelpyle
text: Yes, as long as we did not draw down any of those grant proceeds, no harm, no foul at that point, we would back out. As long as we don't draw down the proceeds, there would not be a penalty.

speaker: Other
text: We would probably include those four in the academy that would start in April. So they would be in there. We just wouldn't be placing people into the SRO program and we would have overhires for, which would be nice for the patrol.

speaker: darrelpyle
text: Yeah, since we have vacancies currently, and we'll just, if the academy started in April, five months, six months to get to the end, and then we'd figure out how many vacancies we had by the time graduation day arrived.

speaker: breeaclark
text: That would seem the easiest way to address this issue for the long-term as well. I do have concerns that we did have projects on a recent ballot that would have supported public safety that also failed. So that's concerning, but I think Council Member Foreman said it correctly, that people want this program and that's fine, but we have to pay for it as well. Something has to give. So if that is the most logical answer to get us in a better financial footing now, then I'm very comfortable moving forward with that. And for everyone watching, I welcome your input. I'm sure we all do on that next step. We've talked about ways to improve the program and to get better data for the program. And so I don't think right now we're discussing, do we like the program or not? We're talking about how do we pay for it? So I would be, again, interested in feedback on that. It sounds like we could do it. I would go ahead and make it a quarter percent. So we're thinking a little bit more long-term and not consistently coming back to vote on this. But I, again, welcome feedback on that to see how we are good fiscal managers for the city of Norman. And again, to get us in the best position possible to pay for the things that our residents want. Any other comments from council for tonight? Questions?

speaker: darrelpyle
text: Council Member Behrman. Oh, I'm sorry. I was just gonna add to the mayor's comments that at the retreat coming up, could be a great discussion topic to put fine points on all of those discussion items from this evening.

speaker: breeaclark
text: Which that reminds me, if you all haven't marked your calendars for October 16th, I told Brenda I would tell you to do that today. You've been put on notice once again. Council Member Behrman.

speaker: katebierman
text: So City Manager Pyle actually kind of stole part of my point there as I was gonna ask, I was gonna ask City Attorney Walker if she believed that there was enough time to get details together so that we could put some fine tuning on it at the retreat or use part of the time at the retreat to work on something like that.

speaker: kathrynwalker
text: Sure, I was digging around trying to find my calendar of election dates. So for a January election, first reading would be on October 27th. I believe you've already postponed something for consideration on that night, also for potentially a January election. For February, it would have to be on first reading on November 24th, March, December 8th, April, January 12th. 2021 is a good year for elections. There's a lot of, maybe every month you can have an election, which is not the case in even numbered years. So there's 11 of the 12 months you can have one. So lots of options.

speaker: katebierman
text: Well, and I'm glad that we have lots of options because one of the things I do want to make sure we do is kind of find that balance between moving expeditiously if council decides to accept this grant contingent on a successful outcome of a vote and also making sure that we can have a pretty comprehensive education campaign because as council member Holman reminded us, this did not have a sweeping majority mandate from Norman residents when it was made permanent in 2015. It only passed by 138 votes, which is not at all dissimilar to how some of our recent propositions turned out in the reverse. So this was not an overwhelming mandate from voters back then. I expect it likely won't be this time. And I want to do right by the information that NPD and Norman Public Schools has generated on this program over the last few years and make sure that we talk about this in a very comprehensive and non-politicized way, which may be very difficult heading into the late fall. So I just, I really want to be sensitive to that and kind of balance those two competing needs while also recognizing that I really, really despise funding things with sales tax. I mean, I know that it's kind of avoidable or it's unavoidable in Oklahoma, but it really concerns me, especially when we all know that we are not too far away from a regional transit authority that is also going to require a fairly substantive sales tax increase. So I just, I feel like this is a very feasible path forward, but I feel like there are a lot of hidden potholes along the way that I really want to be sure that we're able to game out and not rush. So I like where the conversation is going though, and I just wanted to throw those things out there.

speaker: breeaclark
text: That was a fantastic discussion. I think we've done a good job of looking, not just to next year, but the next five years and making sure that we're able to pay our bills. So hopefully City Manager Pyle, you've got some direction and another item for our agenda at the retreat. And I want to thank you. And I want to thank Captain Hawkins for a great presentation. That was very informative. I really appreciate that. And I appreciate being open to our feedback. You can never have enough data. So I think that program does a lot of great things and in the areas that may be not so great, the data will help us capture it all and also improve as Council Member Patron was saying. Mr. Milner, thank you for being here. I'm sure you love the invitation to join Council on Tuesday nights.

speaker: katebierman
text: And Mr. C, congratulations. We're a hood, what are you talking about? We're the place to be on Tuesday nights. They should all be so lucky to sit in Mr. Milner's chair.

speaker: breeaclark
text: There you go. But Mr. C, I'm sorry if I'm messing up your title, but congratulations on getting a grant. I mean, that is something to be proud of. It's just unfortunate that we- Who knew it would be this year? Yeah, I got to be here in the pandemic. It's about par for 2020 in Norman though. So, but thank you all for your time. This was exactly, I think, the conversation that needed to happen. And if we continue to take the grant and our community continues to invest in this program, I would like to not only see the data, but reevaluate, perhaps tweak the MOU that it gets looked at more than just automatically renewed. I think that would be something good for future councils as well. If there are no other questions or comments, we will wrap up tonight's study session. All right, thanks everyone. Have a good night.

speaker: darrelpyle
text: Thank you, Justin. I'll join you at a school board meeting coming up at your choosing. Trade you.
